data.name: Google Spotlight Stories: Pearl
data.detailed_description:
EMMY AWARD-WINNER OUTSTANDING INNOVATION in INTERACTIVE STORYTELLING 2017
ACADEMY AWARD NOMINEE BEST ANIMATED SHORT 2017

Google Spotlight Stories presents Pearl in VR. Set inside their home, a beloved hatchback, Pearl follows a girl and her dad as they crisscross the country chasing their dreams. It’s a story about the gifts we hand down and their power to carry love. And finding grace in the unlikeliest of places.

Directed by Patrick Osborne

Mínimos:
  • Sistema Operativo *: Windows 7 SP1, Windows 8.1 or later, Windows 10
  • Processador: Intel i5-4590, AMD FX 8350 equivalent or better
  • Memória: 4 GB de RAM
  • Placa gráfica: Nvidia GeForce GTX 970, AMD Radeon R9 290 equivalent or better
  • Espaço no disco: Requer 3 GB de espaço livre

  • Compatibilidade com R.V.: SteamVR or Oculus PC. Keyboard and mouse required

reviews.review:
Google Spotlight Stories: Pearl is a very short VR experience that feels more like an animated short than a traditional game. I am placed inside the world of Pearl, following a girl and her dad as they travel around in their old car while their lives change over time. There are no real combat systems, puzzles or complicated objectives here. Instead, I am there to watch the story unfold around me and take in the little details happening in every direction.

The VR presentation is easily the best thing about it. The story takes place around the family home and their car, and I can look around the environment while the characters continue acting around me. I really like this because it makes the experience feel different from simply watching a normal animated film on a screen. The characters are not always directly in front of me, so I actually have to pay attention to what is happening around the scene. That makes the VR format feel like it has a proper reason to exist rather than just being a normal video put into a headset.

The story itself is simple but it has some emotional weight. Pearl follows the relationship between a daughter and her dad as they chase their dreams and deal with changes in their lives. I like that it does not need a huge amount of dialogue to get its point across. The music and animation do a lot of the work, especially as the story moves through different stages of their lives. It is a gentle story about family, memories and the things people pass on to each other, and I think the short format suits it well.

The biggest problem is the lack of interaction. Calling this a game is honestly stretching the definition a little because I am mainly watching an interactive animated story rather than actually playing. There are no meaningful decisions for me to make and there is not much reason to replay it once I have seen everything. That is fine if I approach Pearl as a VR short film, but it does limit how much I can get from it as a game. The experience is also extremely short, so I am finished well before I feel like I have properly settled into the world.

I also have to take the age of the experience into account. Pearl originally released in 2017, and some parts of the VR presentation do not feel quite as impressive now as they probably did when it was newer. There can be moments where the animation does not look perfectly smooth, and the technical requirements are fairly demanding for such a small experience. Still, the art direction has held up better than I expected, and the simple environments work because the focus is always on the characters and the story rather than trying to show off a huge virtual world.

What I appreciate most is that Pearl does not waste its short runtime. It has a clear beginning, middle and ending, and the VR format adds something meaningful to the way I experience the story. It is also completely free, which makes the short length much easier for me to accept. I would not want to pay a normal game price for something this brief, but as a free VR experience I think it is much easier to recommend. It feels like something I can sit through once, enjoy and remember rather than something I am expected to keep playing for hours.

Overall, Google Spotlight Stories: Pearl is a lovely little VR story that succeeds much more as an interactive animated short than as a conventional game. I like the family story, the animation, the music and especially the way the VR environment lets me look around and watch events happen naturally. The lack of real gameplay and extremely short runtime stop it from reaching my higher ratings, but I think the experience is worth having when it costs nothing and only asks for a small amount of my time. For me, it is a good example of how VR can be used to tell a simple story in a more personal way.

Rating: 7.7/10
